cards.text: Psalm 88 is a song of the sons of Korah, a Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite, and Heman is crying out to the LORD. Fair warning, friend: this one is DARK. And I'm saying that as a stamper who lived YEARS in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Heman is hurting. In his very first line, what does he call the LORD?

cards.text: And he's not praying once and calling it a day. He cries out before the LORD day AND night. Friend, I can't even stay awake through one batch of cookies.

cards.question: Heman wants the LORD to hear him. He asks the LORD to incline His ___ to his cry.

cards.text: Then he tells the LORD why he's crying out. His soul is full of troubles, and his life draws near to Sheol.

cards.question: Heman feels his life slipping toward Sheol. Who does he say he's counted among?

answers.text: The elders at the city gate

cards.text: He says he's like a man without strength. Forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave.

cards.question: Heman compares himself to the slain who lie in the grave. True or false: he describes them as people the LORD remembers no more.

cards.text: Now Heman goes further. He doesn't just say where he is. He says who put him there.

cards.question: Heman feels like he's in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths. Who does he say laid him there?

cards.text: And he says the LORD's wrath weighs heavily upon him. That's not a bad day, friend. That's a whole season.

cards.question: Heman feels like he's going under. He says all the LORD's ___ have submerged him.

cards.text: Then it gets personal: Heman says the LORD has removed his friends from him. Friend, even in the junk drawer I had the dead batteries to argue with.

cards.question: Heman's friends are gone. What does he say the LORD has made him to them?
Heman feels shut in. True or false: he says he has found a way to escape.

cards.text: His eyes grow dim with grief, and he STILL shows up. Every day, Heman calls to the LORD.

cards.question: Heman keeps calling to the LORD daily. What does he do with his hands?

answers.text: Spreads them out to the LORD

cards.text: Then Heman starts asking the LORD questions. Hard ones, one after another. This is NOT a how's-your-day-going kind of chat.

cards.question: In Heman's first question, he asks if the LORD works wonders for whom?

cards.text: Next he asks if departed spirits rise up to praise the LORD. Then he asks if His loving devotion can be proclaimed in the grave.

cards.question: Heman's questions keep coming. He asks if the LORD's wonders will be known in the ___.

cards.text: Or His righteousness in the land of oblivion? And right after all those questions comes one small word: But.

cards.question: After all those heavy questions, what does Heman do next?

answers.text: Cries to the LORD for help

cards.text: In the morning, his prayer comes before the LORD. Friend, in the morning I'm still fighting the snooze button, and LOSING.

cards.question: Heman asks the LORD why He rejects him, and why He hides His ___ from him.

cards.text: And this isn't new for Heman. He's been afflicted and near death for a long time.

cards.question: How long has Heman been afflicted and near death?

cards.text: He says he has borne the LORD's terrors and he's in despair. The LORD's wrath has swept over him, and His terrors have destroyed him.

cards.question: Heman says the LORD's terrors engulf him like water. True or false: he says that only happens once in a while.
Heman feels trapped. He says the LORD's terrors enclose him on every ___.

cards.text: Then the last verse. Heman is back to his loved ones being gone: the LORD has removed his beloved and his friend.

cards.question: In Heman's very last line, what does he call his closest companion?
True or false: Psalm 88 ends with Heman bursting into praise.

cards.text: And that's where Psalm 88 ends, friend: in the dark. But Heman kept talking to the LORD the whole way down, and I know a little something about calling out from the dark.

findings.problem: The baker can't reason out what Heman calls the LORD in his opening line. Nothing on card 1 points to 'The God of my salvation' over 'The God of my fathers', so the pick comes down to luck. The question also asks the baker to guess the exact wording of the line.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The God who forgot me' has an emotional, modern tone. The other two answers are biblical titles, so this one stands out from them.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question says 'Heman feels like he's in the lowest Pit'. Verse 6 has no 'like': it says 'You have laid me in the lowest Pit'. The card softens a plain statement into a feeling and a comparison.
The question asks 'Who does he say laid him there?' The wrong answer 'His own sin' is not a who, so it isn't the same kind of thing as 'The LORD' and 'His enemies'.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card cites Psalm 88:13-14 but only tells verse 13b, the morning prayer. Verse 14 is first used on card 8, so the citation should be Psalm 88:13.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says Heman has been afflicted 'for a long time'. That rules out the wrong answers 'Since last spring' and 'For forty days' on card 10 before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says 'I know a little something about calling out from the dark.' In his backstory he went quiet in the drawer and didn't know God until the angel came. Nothing says he called out from the dark, so the line adds something new to his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card tells nothing new from verse 18. Cards 15 and 16 already covered how the psalm ends. The card restates that the psalm ends in the dark and sums up that Heman kept praying, so it works as a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.
